\begin{corollary}[Same-base effective specialization]
\label{cor:same-base-effective-rational-mahler}
Let \(A\) be an \(n\times n\) non-negative integral matrix and let \(B,B'\)
be integral matrices satisfying
\[
 \abs{B_{ij}},\abs{B'_{ij}}\le A_{ij},
 \qquad B_{ij}\equiv B'_{ij}\equiv A_{ij}\pmod2.
\]
Assume that
\(P_0=\det(I-zB)\) and \(P_1=\det(I-zB')\) are coprime, and put
\(a_*=\max\{1,A_{ij}:1\le i,j\le n\}\).  Then the algorithm of
\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} decides and constructs every
normalized rational certificate for \(P_0/P_1\), using integer coefficient
recursion before the Pad\'e step.  Uniformly,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:same-base-effective-input-bounds}
 D\le2n,\qquad N<16n^3,\qquad
 h(P_0),h(P_1)\le n\log(na_*),
\end{equation}
and one may use
\begin{equation}\label{eq:same-base-effective-height-bound}
 K\le N\log2+2n(\lfloor\log_2(2n)\rfloor+1)
       \bigl(2n\log(na_*)+\log(n+1)\bigr).
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The determinant congruence modulo two gives \(P_0\equiv P_1\pmod2\).
For \(0\le k\le n\), expansion by principal minors and domination by the
permanent give
\[
 \abs{[z^k]\det(I-zB)}
 \le\sum_{\substack{I\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}\\|I|=k}}
       \operatorname{per}(A[I,I])
 \le n^ka_*^k\le(na_*)^n,
\]
and the same estimate holds for \(B'\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:same-base-effective-input-bounds}; substituting those inequalities
in \eqref{eq:effective-mahler-height-bound} proves
\eqref{eq:same-base-effective-height-bound}.  Coprimality is stated because
the numerical bounds of \Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} apply
to the reduced input pair.  A non-coprime determinant ratio may first be
cancelled, but no unchanged-height assertion for the uncancelled pair is
being made here.
\end{proof}

This mechanism is strictly weaker than full \(G\)-cospectrality, equivalently
represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
\eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and
\eqref{eq:c2-collision-second-determinant} are different.  Represented
cospectrality in every irreducible representation instead requires equality
of the full twisted spectra and therefore preserves the complete periodic profile
\cite{BoyleSchmieding2017FiniteGroupExtensions,
CavaleriDonno2022Cospectrality}.

We next delimit the finite minimality assertion.  A \emph{regular polynomial
\(C_2\)-certificate} is a tuple \((A,B,B',Q)\) in which \(A\) is a primitive
\(m\)-out-regular integral adjacency matrix, \(B,B'\) are compatible sign
blocks, \(Q\in\ZZ[z]\) is non-constant with \(Q(0)=Q(1/m)=1\), both sign
blocks have spectral radius less than \(m\), and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-polynomial-certificate}
 \det(I-zB)=Q(z^2),
 \qquad
 \det(I-zB')=Q(z)^2.
\end{equation}
Its complexity is ordered lexicographically as
\[
 \bigl(2,\deg Q,|V|,m,|E|\bigr).
\]

\begin{proposition}[Minimality in the regular polynomial certificate class]
\label{prop:c2-certificate-minimality}
The certificate in \Cref{thm:c2-boundary-collision} has complexity
\((2,2,4,4,16)\), and this is the least complexity of a regular polynomial
\(C_2\)-certificate.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first coordinate is fixed by the non-trivial binary group.  Since
\(Q(0)=Q(1/m)=1\), a non-constant \(Q\) cannot have degree one, so
\(\deg Q\ge2\).  If \(\deg Q=2\), then \(Q(z^2)\) has degree four, whereas
\(\deg\det(I-zB)\le |V|\); hence \(|V|\ge4\).

It remains to exclude \(m=2,3\) at \(\deg Q=2\) and \(|V|=4\).  Write
\begin{equation}\label{eq:minimality-q-form}
 Q(z)=1-kz+kmz^2,
 \qquad k\in\ZZ\setminus\{0\},
\end{equation}
which follows from \(Q(1/m)=1\).  When \(m=2\), the characteristic
polynomial forced by the second identity in
\eqref{eq:regular-polynomial-certificate} is
\((x^2-kx+2k)^2\).  If its roots have modulus strictly less than two, their
product gives \(|k|<2\).  The choice \(k=-1\) has a root \(-2\), and
\(k=0\) makes \(Q\) constant; therefore strict gap forces \(k=1\).

There are exactly ten non-negative integral four-entry rows of sum two,
namely \(2e_i\) and \(e_i+e_j\) for \(i<j\).  We exhaust the resulting
\(10^4\) matrices.  Primitivity is decided exactly by testing positivity of
a power through exponent ten, the four-dimensional Wielandt bound.  This
leaves \(2208\) primitive base matrices.  For each such matrix, every
compatible signed entry is enumerated from
\[
 B_{ij}\in\{-A_{ij},-A_{ij}+2,\ldots,A_{ij}\}.
\]
For an integral \(4\times4\) matrix, put \(t_r=\Tr(B^r)\).  Newton's
identities give
\[
 \det(I-zB)=1-t_1z+\frac{t_1^2-t_2}{2}z^2
 -\frac{t_1^3-3t_1t_2+2t_3}{6}z^3+\det(B)z^4.
\]
Thus the two target polynomials
\(1-z^2+2z^4\) and \((1-z+2z^2)^2\) are tested by the integer quadruples
\[
 (t_1,t_2,t_3,\det B)=(0,2,0,2),
 \qquad (2,-6,-10,4),
\]
respectively.  The exhaustive integer enumeration finds \(48\) primitive
bases supporting the first target and no primitive base supporting the
second.  Hence no certificate exists for \(m=2\).  The enumeration and all
counts are reproduced by the exact-arithmetic verifier cited in
\Cref{sec:exactness}.

When \(m=3\), compatibility gives
\(B\mathbf1\equiv A\mathbf1\equiv\mathbf1\pmod2\).  Therefore
\(I-B\) is singular over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\det(I-B)\) is even.  On the
other hand, the first identity in
\eqref{eq:regular-polynomial-certificate} and
\eqref{eq:minimality-q-form} give
\[
 \det(I-B)=Q(1)=1-k+3k=1+2k,
\]
which is odd.  Thus \(m=3\) is impossible.  Since \(m>1\), it follows that
\(m\ge4\), and regularity gives \(|E|=m|V|\ge16\).  The matrices in
\Cref{thm:c2-boundary-collision} attain every bound.
\end{proof}

The minimality assertion is deliberately confined to the finite polynomial
certificate class in \eqref{eq:regular-polynomial-certificate}; it is not a
minimality statement for the rational certificates decided by
\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary}, and it does not address
positive rational functions outside the determinant-parity hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting}.

Although one Perron-point value loses information, an analytic radial profile
restores it.  The following is a sufficient recovery criterion; no optimality
claim about the amount of profile data is intended.

\begin{theorem}[Radial-profile recovery]
\label{thm:radial-profile-recovery}
Let \(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to G\) be two labellings on the same primitive

 succeeded in 231ms:
now show that its existence and the certificate itself are decidable by a
single finite Pad\'e calculation.  For an integral polynomial \(P\), write
\[
 h(P):=\log\max_j\abs{[z^j]P}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Effective normalized rational coboundary criterion]
\label{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary}
Let \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) be coprime, with
\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\).  Put \(d_i=\deg P_i\) and \(D=d_0+d_1\).
If \(D=0\), then \(P_0=P_1=1\), and the unique normalized solution is
\(R=1\).  If \(D>0\), put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-bounds}
 L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
 \qquad
 N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1)<2D^3,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-height-bound}
 \Lambda=h(P_0)+h(P_1)
   +\frac12\log\bigl((d_0+1)(d_1+1)\bigr),
 \qquad
 K=N\log2+D(L+1)\Lambda.
\end{equation}
There is a finite algorithm over \(\QQ\), using only \(P_0,P_1\), which
decides whether
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-equation}
 \frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
 =\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
 \qquad R\in\QQ(z)^\times,\quad R(0)=1,
\end{equation}
and constructs \(R\) when it exists.  The solution is unique.  In its unique
reduced form
\[
 R=\frac{A}{B},
 \qquad A,B\in\ZZ[z],\quad (A,B)=1,\quad A(0)=B(0)=1,
\]
it satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-output-bounds}
 \deg A+\deg B\le N,
 \qquad
 \max\{h(A),h(B)\}\le K.
\end{equation}
In particular, \(\max\{\deg A,\deg B\}<2D^3\).  Two necessary conditions
are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-obstructions}
 d_0=d_1,
 \qquad P_0\equiv P_1\pmod2.
\end{equation}

More explicitly, let \(S(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}s_nz^n\in1+z\QQ[[z]]\) be the
unique formal solution of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-formal-equation}
 P_0(z)S(z)^2=P_1(z)S(z^2).
\end{equation}
Writing \(p_{i,j}=[z^j]P_i\), its coefficients are obtained successively from
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-coefficient-recurrence}
\begin{split}
 2s_n={}&
 \sum_{\substack{0\le j\le d_1\\j\le n,\ n-j\ {\rm even}}}
   p_{1,j}s_{(n-j)/2} \\
 &-\sum_{\substack{0\le j\le d_0,\ u,v\ge0,\ u+v=n-j\\
          (j,u,v)\ne(0,0,n),(0,n,0)}}p_{0,j}s_us_v
 \qquad(n\ge1).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
After computing \(s_0,\ldots,s_{2N}\), solve the affine linear system
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-pade-system}
 \sum_{j=0}^N b_js_{k-j}=0
 \quad(N+1\le k\le2N),
 \qquad b_0=1,\qquad s_m=0\ (m<0).
\end{equation}
If it is inconsistent, reject.  Otherwise choose any solution, put
\[
 B_*(z)=\sum_{j=0}^Nb_jz^j,
 \qquad
 A_*(z)=\sum_{k=0}^N
       \left(\sum_{j=0}^{\min\{k,N\}}b_js_{k-j}\right)z^k,
\]
cancel their common factor, and normalize both constant terms to one.  Accept
the resulting \(A/B\) precisely when
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-final-identity}
 P_0(z)A(z)^2B(z^2)=P_1(z)A(z^2)B(z)^2.
\end{equation}
Thus the procedure requires neither factorization over
\(\overline{\QQ}\) nor enumeration of divisors.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Suppose first that \(R\) exists.  For
\(\alpha\in\overline{\QQ}^{\times}\), set
\[
 r(\alpha)=\operatorname{ord}_{z=\alpha}R,
 \qquad
 e(\alpha)=\operatorname{ord}_{z=\alpha}(P_0/P_1).
\]
The map \(z\mapsto z^2\) is unramified at \(\alpha\ne0\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-divisor-recurrence}
 e(\alpha)=r(\alpha^2)-2r(\alpha).
\end{equation}
Along the forward square orbit, write \(r_j=r(\alpha^{2^j})\) and
\(e_j=e(\alpha^{2^j})\).  Iteration gives
\[
 r_0=2^{-m}r_m-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}2^{-j-1}e_j.
\]
The divisor of \(R\) has finite support, so \(r_m\) is bounded.  Letting
\(m\to\infty\), and using \(\abs{e_j}\le D\), gives
\(\abs{r(\alpha)}\le D\).  If \(r(\alpha)\ne0\), the forward orbit must
meet the support of \(e\).  If \(k\) is its first such index, then
\(r_{j+1}=2r_j\) for \(j<k\); hence
\[
 2^k\le2^k\abs{r_0}=\abs{r_k}\le D,
 \qquad k\le L.
\]
Consequently every finite non-zero zero or pole of \(R\) is a zero of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-window-polynomial}
 W(z):=\prod_{k=0}^{L}P_0(z^{2^k})P_1(z^{2^k}).
\end{equation}
Because each input polynomial is primitive and has constant term one, every
rational irreducible factor of \(W\), normalized to have constant term one,
lies in \(\ZZ[z]\).  The multiplicity bound above therefore gives
\[
 A(z)B(z)\mid W(z)^D\quad\hbox{in }\ZZ[z].
\]
Since
\(\deg W=D(2^{L+1}-1)\), this proves the degree bound in
\eqref{eq:effective-mahler-output-bounds}.

Let \(M(\,\cdot\,)\) denote Mahler measure.  The standard estimates
\[
 \log M(Q)\le h(Q)+\frac12\log(\deg Q+1),
 \qquad
 h(Q)\le\deg Q\log2+\log M(Q)
\]
and \(M(Q(z^m))=M(Q)\) give
\[
 \log M(W)\le(L+1)\Lambda.
\]
Mahler measure is multiplicative, and a non-zero integral polynomial has
measure at least one.  The preceding divisibility thus implies
\[
 \log M(A),\ \log M(B)\le D(L+1)\Lambda.
\]
Together with the degree bound, this proves
\eqref{eq:effective-mahler-height-bound}--
\eqref{eq:effective-mahler-output-bounds}.

At infinity,
\(\operatorname{ord}_\infty R(z^2)=2\operatorname{ord}_\infty R\), so the right-hand side
of \eqref{eq:effective-mahler-equation} has order zero there.  This proves
\(d_0=d_1\).  Moreover, reduction modulo two gives
\(A(z^2)=A(z)^2\) and \(B(z^2)=B(z)^2\).  Hence the right-hand side is one
in \(\mathbb F_2(z)\), proving \(P_0\equiv P_1\pmod2\).

The two occurrences of \(s_n\) on the left of
\eqref{eq:effective-mahler-formal-equation} have coefficient two; every
other coefficient in degree \(n\) involves only
\(s_0,\ldots,s_{n-1}\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:effective-mahler-coefficient-recurrence} and the uniqueness of
\(S\).  If a rational solution exists, its Taylor series is \(S\).  The
degree bound therefore implies that its denominator occurs among the
solutions of \eqref{eq:effective-mahler-pade-system}.

It remains to justify that an arbitrary solution of that system is harmless.
For two resulting pairs \((A_i,B_i)\), one has
\[
 B_iS-A_i=O(z^{2N+1}),
\]
and consequently
\[
 A_1B_2-A_2B_1=O(z^{2N+1}).
\]
The polynomial on the left has degree at most \(2N\), and hence vanishes
identically.  Thus every solution of the affine system produces the same
rational approximant.  If a genuine \(R\) exists, this approximant is \(R\);
conversely, \eqref{eq:effective-mahler-final-identity} is exactly the cleared
form of \eqref{eq:effective-mahler-equation}.  The final identity therefore
gives both sound rejection and complete reconstruction.  Uniqueness also
follows from the normalized injectivity of \(\delta\) proved in
\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Termination and a conservative bit bound]
\label{rem:effective-rational-mahler-complexity}
Let
\[
 d=\max\{1,d_0,d_1\},
 \qquad
 \tau=1+\max_i\left\lceil\log_2\norm{P_i}_\infty\right\rceil,
 \qquad b=\tau+\log(D+1).
\]
All loops stop at \(2N\), and the only linear system has \(N\) equations and
\(N\) unknowns.  If the parity condition in
\eqref{eq:effective-mahler-obstructions} holds, the
Dieudonn\'e--Dwork argument of
\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality} applies verbatim to
\eqref{eq:effective-mahler-formal-equation}, so \(S\in\ZZ[[z]]\).  On the
circle
\[
 \abs z=\rho:=(4d2^\tau)^{-1}
\]
one has \(\abs{P_i(z)-1}\le1/4\).  The convergent local product for \(S\)
is
\[
 S(z)=\prod_{\nu\ge0}
 \left(\frac{P_1(z^{2^\nu})}{P_0(z^{2^\nu})}\right)^{2^{-\nu-1}}.
\]
Indeed,
\[
 \abs{P_i(z)-1}
 \le\frac{d2^{\tau-1}\rho}{1-\rho}<\frac14,
\]
and the logarithm series gives
\(\abs{\log S(z)}\le2\log(4/3)<\log2\).  Thus
\(\abs{S(z)}<2\) on the circle, and Cauchy's estimate gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-coefficient-size}
 \abs{s_n}\le2(4d2^\tau)^n.
\end{equation}
Thus the required series coefficients have \(O(Nb)\) bits.  In Bareiss
fraction-free elimination, every intermediate entry is a minor and has
\(O(N^2b)\) bits.  With schoolbook integer arithmetic, the complete procedure
therefore uses
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-mahler-bit-complexity}
 O(N^7b^2)\quad\hbox{bit operations},
 \qquad O(N^4b)\quad\hbox{bits of storage}.
\end{equation}
These deliberately elementary bounds prove polynomial-time termination; no
claim of optimality is made.  Fast integer and modular linear algebra improve
them, but an exact sharper exponent would require a separate complexity
analysis.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Same-base effective specialization]
\label{cor:same-base-effective-rational-mahler}
Let \(A\) be an \(n\times n\) non-negative integral matrix and let \(B,B'\)
be integral matrices satisfying

 succeeded in 249ms:
\(\operatorname{Pic}^0(\mathbb P^1_{\QQ})=0\), choose
\(S\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with \(\operatorname{div}S=D\), normalized by
\(S(0)=1\).  Then \(Q/S^m\) is constant, and evaluation at zero gives
\(Q=S^m\).  It follows that \((H/\delta S)^m=1\).  This rational function is
constant and has value one at zero, so \(H=\delta S\); take \(R=S\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Algebraic critical products are rational coboundaries]
\label{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}
Let \(H\in\QQ(z)^\times\), \(H(0)=1\), and suppose that
\(F\in1+z\QQ[[z]]\) is algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfies
\(F(z)^2=H(z)F(z^2)\).  Then \(H=\delta R\) for a unique
\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with \(R(0)=1\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put \(G=zF'/F\).  Logarithmic differentiation gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:log-derivative-mahler}
 G(z)=G(z^2)+\frac z2\frac{H'(z)}{H(z)}.
\end{equation}
If the rational inhomogeneous term is non-zero, the equations at \(z\) and
\(z^2\) eliminate it to give a homogeneous scalar \(2\)-Mahler equation for
\(G\); if it is zero, \eqref{eq:log-derivative-mahler} and \(G(0)=0\) give
\(G=0\).  Since algebraic functions are D-finite, B\'ezivin's theorem that a
D-finite Mahler function is rational
\cite[Theorem~1]{BellCoonsRowland2013MahlerDichotomy} yields
\(G\in\CC(z)\), and its rational Taylor coefficients give
\(G\in\QQ(z)\).

All analytic branches of the algebraic function \(F\) have the same rational
logarithmic derivative, so their pairwise quotients are constants.  Finite
monodromy therefore gives an \(m\ge1\) for which
\(T=F^m\) is single-valued, hence \(T\in\CC(z)^\times\).  Its Taylor
coefficients give \(T\in\QQ(z)^\times\), and \(T(0)=1\).  Raising the
functional equation to the \(m\)-th power gives
\[
 H^m=\frac{T(z)^2}{T(z^2)}=\delta(T^{-1}).
\]
Apply \Cref{lem:rational-mahler-saturation}, and then use the normalized
injectivity proved in \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} for uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strict-gap determinant boundary lifting]
\label{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting}
Let \(A\) be a primitive non-negative integer matrix with Perron root
\(\lambda>1\), and put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\).  Let \(B,B'\) be integer matrices
of the same size such that, entrywise,
\[
 \abs{B_{ij}},\abs{B'_{ij}}\le A_{ij},
 \qquad B_{ij}\equiv B'_{ij}\equiv A_{ij}\pmod2,
\]
and suppose that \(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\).  Set
\[
 H(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}.
\]
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
 \item \(\Pi_x(H)=1\);
 \item there is a unique \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
 \[
  R(0)=R(x)=1,
  \qquad H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2}.
 \]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The strict gaps imply that both determinant polynomials are non-zero on a disk
\(\abs z<r\) for some \(x<r<1\).  They are positive on \([0,x]\), because
they are real, non-zero there, and equal one at zero.  Hence \(H>0\) on that
interval.  Define \(F\) by \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-product}.  By
\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, it is analytic on \(\abs z<r\), has
integer coefficients, and satisfies \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-equation}.
Crucially, the product normalization is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
 F(x)^2=\Pi_x(H),
\end{equation}
not \(F(x)=\Pi_x(H)\).

We now verify every hypothesis of Nishioka's special-value theorem
\cite[Theorem, p.~387]{Nishioka1982MahlerFunctionValues}.  Write the rational
function \(H\) in reduced form
\[
 H=\frac{\widehat P_0}{\widehat P_1},
 \qquad
 \widehat P_0,\widehat P_1\in\ZZ[z],
 \qquad
 \gcd(\widehat P_0,\widehat P_1)=1,
 \qquad
 \widehat P_0(0)=\widehat P_1(0)=1.
\]
The common factors removed here do not affect zero-freeness on \(\abs z<r\).
In the notation of the cited theorem, take
\[
 Tz=z^2,
 \qquad
 Q_0(z,u)=\widehat P_0(z),
 \qquad
 Q_1(z,u)=-\widehat P_1(z)u^2.
\]
Then the functional equation is exactly
\[
 Q_0(z,F(z))F(Tz)+Q_1(z,F(z))=0.
\]
The two polynomials \(Q_0,Q_1\) are relatively prime in
\(\overline{\QQ}[z,u]\): a common factor cannot contain \(u\), since
\(\widehat P_0(0)=1\), and the remaining assertion is the displayed
coprimality of \(\widehat P_0,\widehat P_1\).  Nishioka's auxiliary
polynomial \(g(z)\), obtained as a polynomial combination of the \(Q_i\)
and independent of \(u\), may therefore be chosen simply as
\(g(z)=Q_0(z,u)=\widehat P_0(z)\).

The numerical parameters are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
  p&=2, & N&=0, & n&=1, & m&=2,\\
  M&=\max\{p+N,m\}=2, & U&=1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus, with coefficient-growth exponent \(L=1\), her strict inequality is
\[
 M(p+N)n^2=2\cdot2\cdot1=4
 <2^{2+1/L}=8.
\]
It remains to check the arithmetic and orbit conditions, rather than merely
record the parameters.  Write \(F(z)=\sum_{h\ge0}a_hz^h\).  By
\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, all \(a_h\) lie in the fixed number
field \(\QQ\) and are algebraic integers.  Choose \(s\) with \(x<s<r\).
Cauchy's estimate on \(\abs z=s\) gives
\[
 \abs{a_h}\le \max_{\abs z=s}\abs{F(z)}\,s^{-h}.
\]
Hence Nishioka's coefficient-size and common-denominator bounds hold with
\(L=1\): the denominators are one and the logarithmic coefficient height is
at most linear in \(h\).  The evaluation point \(x=\lambda^{-1}\) is a
non-zero algebraic number and \(0<Ux<1\).  Moreover,
\[
 T^i x=x^{2^i}\ne0,
 \qquad
 g(T^i x)=\widehat P_0(x^{2^i})\ne0
 \quad(i\ge0),
\]
because \(0<x^{2^i}\le x<r\) and the reduced numerator is zero-free on
\(\abs z<r\).  Finally \(F(x)\) converges because \(F\) is analytic there.
All hypotheses of the cited theorem are therefore satisfied.  It follows
that if \(F\) were transcendental over \(\CC(z)\), then \(F(x)\) would be
transcendental.

Assume \(\textup{(i)}\).  Positivity and \eqref{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
give \(F(x)=1\), so the cited theorem forces \(F\) to be algebraic.  By
\Cref{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}, \(H=\delta R\) for the unique
normalized rational \(R\).  Now
\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} gives
\(1=\Pi_x(H)=R(x)^{-2}\) and \(R(x)>0\), hence \(R(x)=1\).  This proves
\(\textup{(ii)}\).  Conversely, \(\textup{(ii)}\) and
\eqref{eq:rational-mahler-telescope} give \(\textup{(i)}\), and the
same proposition gives uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope of the lifting theorem]
The determinant parity in \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} is essential
to the integrality step, so the theorem does not assert the converse for an
arbitrary positive rational \(H\).  Its realizable class is nevertheless broad.
Fix \(r\ge2\), an odd \(a>0\), and a positive even \(b\), and let \(A\) have
diagonal entries \(a\) and off-diagonal entries \(b\).  Then
\(\lambda=a+(r-1)b\).  Any diagonal \(B=\operatorname{diag}(c_i)\) and
\(B'=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\), with odd
\(\abs{c_i},\abs{d_i}\le a\), satisfies the same-base compatibility and
strict gaps, and realizes
\[
 H(z)=\frac{\prod_i(1-c_i z)}{\prod_i(1-d_i z)}.
\]
\end{remark}

The preceding lifting theorem supplies a rational certificate abstractly.  We
now show that its existence and the certificate itself are decidable by a
single finite Pad\'e calculation.  For an integral polynomial \(P\), write
\[
 h(P):=\log\max_j\abs{[z^j]P}.
\]

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

The theorem of Mohamed and Noorani requires two independent corrections.
Primitivity of the base does not imply Frobenius equidistribution: the
trivial \(C_2\)-cocycle shows that an extension-level
transitivity/aperiodicity condition is necessary.  Under the strict twisted
gap used here, the exponent is \(|C|/|G|\).  At the constant level, the
Frobenius-class product fixes the primitive label \(g_\gamma\), whereas the
periodic Artin logarithm replaces it by \(g_\gamma^r\) on the \(r\)-fold
traversal.  The correct coordinate is therefore \(F_\rho\), with the
finite-determinant formula in \eqref{eq:perron-fixed-determinant}; the strict-gap
\(S_3\) sign channel proves that it cannot generally be replaced by
\(L_\rho\).

The discrepancy is universal at the identity class, not confined to the
\(S_3\) witness.  The quotient-cover factor in
\eqref{eq:identity-class-universal-error} is strictly greater than one for
every non-trivial strict-gap extension and records precisely the primitive
orbits whose lifts close only after repeated traversal.  After the constant is
corrected, \eqref{eq:harmonic-renormalized-product} separates the universal
harmonic factor from an exponentially small system-dependent remainder.

The vector of corrected constants is nevertheless not an inverse invariant
of the primitive class profile.  The fixed-graph \(C_2\) pair in
\Cref{thm:c2-boundary-collision} has different length-one data but identical
constants, because the dyadic boundary functional annihilates a non-trivial
determinant coboundary at the Perron point.  This collision is strictly weaker
than full \(G\)-cospectrality.  In the realizable same-base strict-gap
determinant-ratio class, \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} identifies this
kernel exactly with the normalized rational coboundaries; its parity hypothesis
prevents an extension of that statement here to arbitrary positive rational
functions.  Within its coprime polynomial input class,
\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} decides this rational
coboundary condition by one finite Pad\'e system and supplies explicit output
bounds; \Cref{cor:same-base-effective-rational-mahler} records the compatible
matrix specialization.  Retaining an analytic radial profile
on a set with an interior accumulation point removes the loss by
\Cref{thm:radial-profile-recovery}; no claim of minimality is attached to that
analytic enhancement.

For a homogeneous union of classes, the downstream constant is
\eqref{eq:homogeneous-union-constant}.  The M\"obius transform used to obtain
it is standard necklace/Witt calculus; the paper-specific point is its use on
the fixed-label coordinate before Adams powering.  The appendices record only
the determinant-derived radial convention and established periodic-data and

\section{Boundary-point collisions and radial recovery}
\label{sec:boundary-collisions}

The full represented determinant family determines the primitive
length--class profile by \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary}.  The vector of
class-product constants is substantially coarser: it retains only one radial
value of each non-trivial fixed-label coordinate.  We make this loss explicit
on a fixed base graph.

\begin{theorem}[Exact boundary collision on a fixed \(C_2\)-extension]
\label{thm:c2-boundary-collision}
Let \(G=C_2=\{e,s\}\), with non-trivial character
\(\varepsilon(s)=-1\), and let the base adjacency matrix be
\[
 A=\begin{pmatrix}
 0&4&0&0\\
 1&1&0&2\\
 0&0&0&4\\
 0&2&1&1
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
There are two labellings \(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) on the same marked
directed multigraph whose sign blocks are respectively
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}
 0&-2&0&0\\
 -1&-1&0&-2\\
 0&0&0&-2\\
 0&2&-1&1
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 B'=\begin{pmatrix}
 0&-4&0&0\\
 1&1&0&0\\
 0&0&0&-4\\
 0&0&1&1
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both labellings satisfy the strict twisted gap, and all their class-product
constants agree:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-collision-constants}
 K_{\{e\}}^\tau=K_{\{e\}}^{\tau'},
 \qquad
 K_{\{s\}}^\tau=K_{\{s\}}^{\tau'}.
\end{equation}
Nevertheless, their length-one primitive data are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-collision-length-one}
 \bigl(p_{1,\{e\}}(\tau),p_{1,\{s\}}(\tau)\bigr)=(1,1),
 \qquad
 \bigl(p_{1,\{e\}}(\tau'),p_{1,\{s\}}(\tau')\bigr)=(2,0).
\end{equation}
In particular, equality of all Frobenius-class Mertens constants does not
determine the primitive length--class profile, even when the graph and group
are fixed and both extensions satisfy the strict gap.  The two labellings are
not related by vertex switching and global conjugacy.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every row of \(A\) has sum four.  The underlying directed graph is strongly
connected and has loops, so \(A\) is primitive and \(\lambda=4\).  For each
entry, the numbers of \(e\)- and \(s\)-labelled edges are
\[
 \frac{A_{ij}+B_{ij}}2,\qquad \frac{A_{ij}-B_{ij}}2
\]
for \(\tau\), and the same formulas with \(B'\) for \(\tau'\).  Inspection
shows that these are non-negative integers.  Thus the displayed matrices are
realized on the same marked collection of parallel edges.

Put \(Q(z)=1-z+4z^2\).  Exact determinant calculation gives
\begin{align}
 \det(I-zB)&=1-z^2+4z^4=Q(z^2),
 \label{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant}\\
 \det(I-zB')&=1-2z+9z^2-8z^3+16z^4=Q(z)^2.
 \label{eq:c2-collision-second-determinant}
\end{align}
The characteristic polynomials are
\[
 \det(xI-B)=x^4-x^2+4,
 \qquad
 \det(xI-B')=(x^2-x+4)^2.
\]
For the first polynomial, the substitution \(y=x^2\) shows that
\(y\overline y=4\), hence every root has modulus \(\sqrt2\).  The roots of
\(x^2-x+4\) have modulus two.  Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-collision-gaps}
 \rad(B)=\sqrt2<4,
 \qquad
 \rad(B')=2<4.
\end{equation}

Write \(L_B(z)=-\log\det(I-zB)\) and define \(L_{B'}\) similarly, with the
germs normalized at zero.  In \(C_2\),
\(\psi^m\varepsilon=\varepsilon\) for odd \(m\) and
\(\psi^m\varepsilon=\mathbf1\) for even \(m\).  Since the trivial block is
the same for the two labellings, \eqref{eq:fixed-adams-mobius} gives, first on
\(|z|<1/4\),
\begin{align}
 F_{\varepsilon}^{\tau}(z)-F_{\varepsilon}^{\tau'}(z)
 &=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k
   \left(\sum_{\substack{m\mid k\\m\ \mathrm{odd}}}\mu(m)\right)
   \bigl(L_B(z^k)-L_{B'}(z^k)\bigr)\notag\\
 &=\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}
   \bigl(L_B(z^{2^j})-L_{B'}(z^{2^j})\bigr).
 \label{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}
\end{align}
Here the odd-divisor M\"obius sum is one when \(k\) is a power of two and
zero otherwise.  If \(q_j=\log Q(z^{2^j})\), then
\eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant}--
\eqref{eq:c2-collision-second-determinant} turn the last series into
\[
 \sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}(2q_j-q_{j+1})=2q_0.
\]
The series converges absolutely up to \(0\le z\le1/4\), since
\(q_j=O(z^{2^j})\).  Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-collision-exact-difference}
 F_{\varepsilon}^{\tau}(z)-F_{\varepsilon}^{\tau'}(z)
 =2\log Q(z)\qquad(0\le z\le1/4).
\end{equation}
Because \(Q(1/4)=1\), the two sign coordinates agree at the Perron point.
The base matrix, and hence the scalar terms \(\gamma+\log C(A)\), are also
identical.  Formula \eqref{eq:correct-product-fourier} now proves
\eqref{eq:c2-collision-constants}.  For reference, direct reduction gives
\[
 \det(I-zA)=(1-4z)(1+2z-3z^2-4z^3),
 \qquad C(A)=\frac45.
\]

The only length-one primitive orbits are the loops at vertices two and four.
Their signs are respectively \((-1,1)\) for \(B\) and \((1,1)\) for \(B'\),
which proves \eqref{eq:c2-collision-length-one}.  Finally, vertex switching
acts on a sign block by diagonal sign conjugacy and leaves every loop label
unchanged.  Global conjugacy is trivial in \(C_2\).  Thus the two labellings
cannot be switching--conjugate.  Equivalently, their distinct characteristic
polynomials already preclude diagonal similarity.
\end{proof}

The telescoping in the proof is an exact kernel identity, rather than a
coincidence detected by truncation.

Let \(0<x<1\), and let \(Q\) be a polynomial with \(Q(0)=1\) and no zero on
the radial segment \([0,x]\).  Use the logarithm germ continued from zero
along that segment and define

# Reproducing the exact S3 certificate

The manuscript prints a self-contained rational proof of the interval for
`F_epsilon(1/2)`. The program below independently reproduces the logarithm
brackets, rational tails, and final comparisons.

## Permanent source

Repository:

https://github.com/the-omega-institute/automath

Content-addressed program URL:

https://github.com/the-omega-institute/automath/blob/27d7e8fa74de6860723b81cd5cc3b01139909be7/papers/publication/2026_finite_parts_dynamical_zeta_shifts_finite_type_etds/certificates/s3_log_certificates.py

Program SHA-256:

```text
301737D892108D115F6F70128D03EBF6291F9E91D5811306E7D8A49F915D510C
```

## Environment

- Python 3.11 or later
- SymPy 1.13.1
- Run commands from the manuscript directory

Install the only non-standard dependency:

```powershell
python -m pip install "sympy==1.13.1"
```

## Verification

Run:

```powershell
python certificates/s3_log_certificates.py
```

The program exits with status zero and ends with:

```text
fixed-label windows verified
```

To regenerate the stored plain-text certificate:

```powershell
python certificates/s3_log_certificates.py --write-cert certificates/s3_log_certificates.cert
```

The calculation uses exact rational arithmetic. No floating-point root or
logarithm approximation is used as certificate evidence.

## Boundary collision, minimality, quotient, harmonic, and Fourier checks

The additional exact verification enumerates primitive binary necklaces in a
strict-gap `C2` extension, compares the quotient split-orbit correction with
the periodic-minus-fixed power series through degree 16, derives the universal

\title[Adams-corrected Frobenius products]{Adams-corrected Frobenius-class product constants for finite-group extensions of one-sided shifts of finite type}

\author[Haobo Ma]{Haobo Ma}
\address{AELF PTE. LTD., \#14-02, Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 1,
8 Marina Boulevard, Singapore 018981, Singapore}
\email{auric@aelf.io}
\author[Wenlin Zhang]{Wenlin Zhang}
\address{National University of Singapore, 21 Lower Kent Ridge Road,
Singapore 119077, Singapore}
\email{e1327962@u.nus.edu}
\thanks{Corresponding author: Wenlin Zhang.}
\date{}
\renewcommand{\shortauthors}{H. Ma and W. Zhang}

\begin{document}

\begin{abstract}
Let \(X_\Gamma^+\) be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let \(G\) be finite,
and let a one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit \(\gamma\) by a
conjugacy class \([g_\gamma]\).  We determine the constant in the
Frobenius-class Mertens product by separating two logarithms that coincide in
the scalar theory but not for general finite groups.  The periodic Artin
logarithm repeats both the orbit and its label,
\[
 L_\rho(z)=\sum_{r\geq1}\Pi_{\psi^r\chi_\rho}(z^r)/r,
 \qquad (\psi^r\chi_\rho)(g)=\chi_\rho(g^r),
\]
whereas the class product repeats the scalar weight while keeping the
primitive label fixed.  Its coordinate is therefore
\(F_\rho(z)=\sum_{r\geq1}\Pi_{\chi_\rho}(z^r)/r\).  Under the strict twisted
spectral gap, we prove an Adams--M\"obius determinant formula for
\(F_\rho(\lambda^{-1})\) and hence for every class-product constant.

This corrects two independent defects in the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani
(1999).  First, mixing of the base alone does not imply Frobenius
equidistribution: an extension-level aperiodicity condition, imposed here as
the strict twisted gap, is also necessary.  Second, their constant replaces
\(\chi_\rho(g_\gamma)\) by \(\chi_\rho(g_\gamma^r)\) in the \(r\)-th
logarithmic term.  A trivial \(C_2\)-cocycle disproves the exponent under base
mixing alone, while a strict-gap \(S_3\) extension disproves the asserted
Artin coordinate.  Under the stated gap hypothesis the exponent is
\(|C|/|G|\), and the non-trivial constant coordinates are the fixed-label
values above.  We further identify the exact positive quotient-cover factor
missed by the Artin substitution, proving that it strictly underestimates the
identity-class constant in every non-trivial strict-gap extension.  Harmonic
renormalization gives an exponentially accurate product asymptotic for every
union of Frobenius classes.  Finally, an exact four-vertex \(C_2\) pair shows
that all class constants together do not determine the primitive class
profile, even under strict gap; an analytic radial profile with an interior
accumulation set restores that profile.
\end{abstract}

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

## Why Order Matters

**"I'll write tests after to verify it works"**

Tests written after code pass immediately. Passing immediately proves nothing:
- Might test wrong thing
- Might test implementation, not behavior
- Might miss edge cases you forgot
- You never saw it catch the bug

Test-first forces you to see the test fail, proving it actually tests something.

**"I already manually tested all the edge cases"**

Manual testing is ad-hoc. You think you tested everything but:
- No record of what you tested
- Can't re-run when code changes
- Easy to forget cases under pressure
- "It worked when I tried it" â‰  comprehensive

Automated tests are systematic. They run the same way every time.

**"Deleting X hours of work is wasteful"**

Sunk cost fallacy. The time is already gone. Your choice now:
- Delete and rewrite with TDD (X more hours, high confidence)
- Keep it and add tests after (30 min, low confidence, likely bugs)

The "waste" is keeping code you can't trust. Working code without real tests is technical debt.

**"TDD is dogmatic, being pragmatic means adapting"**

TDD IS pragmatic:
- Finds bugs before commit (faster than debugging after)
- Prevents regressions (tests catch breaks immediately)
- Documents behavior (tests show how to use code)
- Enables refactoring (change freely, tests catch breaks)

"Pragmatic" shortcuts = debugging in production = slower.

**"Tests after achieve the same goals - it's spirit not ritual"**

No. Tests-after answer "What does this do?" Tests-first answer "What should this do?"

Tests-after are biased by your implementation. You test what you built, not what's required. You verify remembered edge cases, not discovered ones.

Tests-first force edge case discovery before implementing. Tests-after verify you remembered everything (you didn't).

30 minutes of tests after â‰  TDD. You get coverage, lose proof tests work.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests passing immediately prove nothing. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals" | Tests-after = "what does this do?" Tests-first = "what should this do?" |
| "Already manually tested" | Ad-hoc â‰  systematic. No record, can't re-run. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy. Keeping unverified code is technical debt. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD faster than debugging. Pragmatic = test-first. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Testing Anti-Patterns

When adding mocks or test utilities, read @testing-anti-patterns.md to avoid common pitfalls:
- Testing mock behavior instead of real behavior
- Adding test-only methods to production classes
- Mocking without understanding dependencies

## Final Rule

```
Production code â†’ test exists and failed first
Otherwise â†’ not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

def _constant_one_polynomial(expression: sp.Expr, variable: sp.Symbol) -> sp.Poly:
    polynomial = sp.Poly(expression, variable, domain=sp.QQ)
    constant = polynomial.eval(0)
    if constant == 0:
        raise ValueError("the polynomial must be non-zero at the origin")
    return sp.Poly(polynomial.as_expr() / constant, variable, domain=sp.QQ)


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr, p_one_expression: sp.Expr
) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int] | None:
    """Decide P0/P1=R(z^2)/R(z)^2 by the finite Pade criterion."""
    z = sp.Symbol("z")
    p_zero = sp.Poly(p_zero_expression, z, domain=sp.ZZ)
    p_one = sp.Poly(p_one_expression, z, domain=sp.ZZ)
    if p_zero.eval(0) != 1 or p_one.eval(0) != 1:
        raise ValueError("both input polynomials must have constant term one")
    if sp.gcd(p_zero, p_one).degree() > 0:
        raise ValueError("the input polynomials must be coprime")

    total_degree = p_zero.degree() + p_one.degree()
    if total_degree == 0:
        return {
            "rational_function": sp.Integer(1),
            "numerator": sp.Integer(1),
            "denominator": sp.Integer(1),
            "degree_bound": 0,
            "height_bound": sp.Integer(0),
        }
    if p_zero.degree() != p_one.degree():
        return None
    maximum_degree = max(p_zero.degree(), p_one.degree())
    if any(
        (p_zero.nth(index) - p_one.nth(index)) % 2
        for index in range(maximum_degree + 1)
    ):
        return None

    logarithmic_depth = total_degree.bit_length() - 1
    degree_bound = total_degree**2 * (2 ** (logarithmic_depth + 1) - 1)
    p_zero_coefficients = [
        p_zero.nth(index) for index in range(p_zero.degree() + 1)
    ]
    p_one_coefficients = [
        p_one.nth(index) for index in range(p_one.degree() + 1)
    ]
    series_coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
    for degree in range(1, 2 * degree_bound + 1):
        right_hand_side = sum(
            p_one_coefficients[index] * series_coefficients[(degree - index) // 2]
            for index in range(min(degree, p_one.degree()) + 1)
            if (degree - index) % 2 == 0
        )
        known_square = sp.Integer(0)
        for index in range(min(degree, p_zero.degree()) + 1):
            residual_degree = degree - index
            for left_degree in range(residual_degree + 1):
                right_degree = residual_degree - left_degree
                if index == 0 and (
                    (left_degree == 0 and right_degree == degree)
                    or (left_degree == degree and right_degree == 0)
                ):
                    continue
                known_square += (
                    p_zero_coefficients[index]
                    * series_coefficients[left_degree]
                    * series_coefficients[right_degree]
                )
        series_coefficients.append(sp.cancel((right_hand_side - known_square) / 2))

    denominator_variables = sp.symbols(f"b1:{degree_bound + 1}")
    denominator_coefficients = (sp.Integer(1),) + denominator_variables
    pade_equations = [
        sum(
            denominator_coefficients[index] * series_coefficients[degree - index]
            for index in range(degree_bound + 1)
        )
        for degree in range(degree_bound + 1, 2 * degree_bound + 1)
    ]
    solution_set = sp.linsolve(pade_equations, denominator_variables)
    if solution_set == sp.EmptySet:
        return None
    solution = next(iter(solution_set))
    free_variables = set().union(*(entry.free_symbols for entry in solution))
    specialization = {variable: 0 for variable in free_variables}
    denominator_coefficients = (sp.Integer(1),) + tuple(
        sp.cancel(entry.subs(specialization)) for entry in solution
    )
    denominator = sum(
        coefficient * z**degree
        for degree, coefficient in enumerate(denominator_coefficients)
    )
    numerator = sum(
        sum(
            denominator_coefficients[index] * series_coefficients[degree - index]
            for index in range(min(degree, degree_bound) + 1)
        )
        * z**degree
        for degree in range(degree_bound + 1)
    )
    numerator, denominator = sp.cancel(numerator / denominator).as_numer_denom()
    numerator = _constant_one_polynomial(numerator, z).as_expr()
    denominator = _constant_one_polynomial(denominator, z).as_expr()
    identity = sp.expand(
        p_zero.as_expr() * numerator**2 * denominator.subs(z, z**2)
        - p_one.as_expr() * numerator.subs(z, z**2) * denominator**2
    )
    if identity != 0:
        return None

    heights = [
        sp.log(max(abs(coefficient) for coefficient in polynomial.all_coeffs()))
        for polynomial in (p_zero, p_one)
    ]
    mahler_input_bound = (
        sum(heights)
        + sp.log((p_zero.degree() + 1) * (p_one.degree() + 1)) / 2
    )
    height_bound = (
        degree_bound * sp.log(2)
        + total_degree * (logarithmic_depth + 1) * mahler_input_bound
    )
    return {
        "rational_function": sp.cancel(numerator / denominator),
        "numerator": numerator,
        "denominator": denominator,
        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
        "height_bound": height_bound,
    }


def effective_mahler_bounds_match() -> bool:
    """Check reconstruction, parity, and the explicit degree/height bounds."""
    z = sp.Symbol("z")
    examples = (1 - z, 1 + 2 * z)
    for rational_function in examples:
        ratio = sp.cancel(
            rational_function.subs(z, z**2) / rational_function**2
        )
        p_zero, p_one = ratio.as_numer_denom()
        p_zero = _constant_one_polynomial(p_zero, z).as_expr()
        p_one = _constant_one_polynomial(p_one, z).as_expr()
        result = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(p_zero, p_one)
        if result is None or result["rational_function"] != rational_function:
            return False
        numerator = sp.Poly(result["numerator"], z, domain=sp.ZZ)
        denominator = sp.Poly(result["denominator"], z, domain=sp.ZZ)
        actual_height = max(
            sp.log(max(abs(coefficient) for coefficient in polynomial.all_coeffs()))
            for polynomial in (numerator, denominator)
        )
        if not all(
            (
                numerator.degree() + denominator.degree()
                <= result["degree_bound"],
                sp.N(actual_height - result["height_bound"], 30) <= 0,
                sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z, modulus=2).is_zero,
            )
        ):
            return False
    return effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(1 + 2 * z, 1 - 2 * z) is None


def same_base_determinant_bounds_match() -> bool:
    """Check the coefficient estimate for compatible same-base sign blocks."""
    z = sp.Symbol("z")
    adjacency = sp.Matrix(
        ((0, 4, 0, 0), (1, 1, 0, 2), (0, 0, 0, 4), (0, 2, 1, 1))
    )
    sign_blocks = (
        sp.Matrix(((0, -2, 0, 0), (-1, -1, 0, -2), (0, 0, 0, -2), (0, 2, -1, 1))),
        sp.Matrix(((0, -4, 0, 0), (1, 1, 0, 0), (0, 0, 0, -4), (0, 0, 1, 1))),
    )
    size = adjacency.rows
    maximum_entry = max(1, *(int(entry) for entry in adjacency))

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        collision_points: tuple[sp.Expr, ...] = ()
+    else:
+        roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+        collision_points = tuple(
+            root
+            for root in roots
+            if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+        )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound + 1,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= degree_bound,
+    }

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(

+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""

+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        collision_points: tuple[sp.Expr, ...] = ()
+    else:
+        roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+        collision_points = tuple(
+            root
+            for root in roots
+            if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+        )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound + 1,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= degree_bound,
+    }
+

\cite{MetropolisRota1983Necklaces}.  The point specific to the present problem
is that a Frobenius-class product retains the fixed primitive label before the
Adams power operation is applied.  Applying the classical transform to this
fixed-label coordinate and then to the finite twisted-determinant family gives
the formulas below.

\begin{theorem}[Primitive and fixed-label determinant coordinates]
\label{thm:adams-mobius}
For every class function \(\phi\) and \(|z|<\lambda^{-1}\),
\begin{align}
  \Pi_\phi(z)
    &=\sum_{m\geq1}\frac{\mu(m)}{m}
       L_{\psi^m\phi}(z^m),
       \label{eq:primitive-adams-mobius}\\
  F_\phi(z):=\sum_{r\geq1}\frac{\Pi_\phi(z^r)}{r}
    &=\sum_{r,m\geq1}\frac{\mu(m)}{rm}
       L_{\psi^m\phi}(z^{rm}).
       \label{eq:fixed-adams-mobius}
\end{align}
For \(\phi=\chi_\rho\), insertion of \eqref{eq:adams-coefficients} gives a
formula involving only the finite determinant family:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-determinant-open-disc}
  F_{\chi_\rho}(z)=
  \sum_{r,m\geq1}\frac{\mu(m)}{rm}
    \sum_{\pi\in\Irr(G)}a_{\rho,\pi}^{(m)}
      \bigl(-\Log_0P_\pi(z^{rm})\bigr).
\end{equation}
All three series are absolutely convergent on compact subsets of the Perron
disc after expansion into primitive orbits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{lem:trace-log},
\[
  L_{\psi^m\phi}(z^m)
  =\sum_{\gamma\in\cP}\sum_{r\geq1}
     \frac{\phi(g_\gamma^{mr})}{r}z^{mr|\gamma|}.
\]
Multiplying by \(\mu(m)/m\), summing, and putting \(s=mr\), the coefficient
of \(\phi(g_\gamma^s)z^{s|\gamma|}\) becomes
\[
  \sum_{m\mid s}\frac{\mu(m)}{m(s/m)}
  =\frac1s\sum_{m\mid s}\mu(m).
\]
It is one for \(s=1\) and zero otherwise.  This proves
\eqref{eq:primitive-adams-mobius}.  Summing that identity over \(z^r/r\)
proves \eqref{eq:fixed-adams-mobius}.  Finally use the character expansion
\eqref{eq:adams-coefficients} and \eqref{eq:artin-determinant-log}.

For convergence, the total number \(p_n\) of primitive length-\(n\) orbits
satisfies \(p_n\leq\Tr(A^n)/n\ll\lambda^n/n\).  Thus the orbit expansions
are dominated on \(|z|\leq R<\lambda^{-1}\) by convergent logarithmic series.
This also justifies every rearrangement above.
\end{proof}

formal rather than terminological.

\begin{proposition}[Standard periodic-data dictionary]
\label{prop:comparison-dictionary}
For two labellings \(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to G\) on the same marked directed
multigraph, the following data are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
 \item \(P_{\rho,\tau}=P_{\rho,\tau'}\) for every
   \(\rho\in\Irr(G)\);
 \item \(\Tr(A_{\rho,\tau}^n)=\Tr(A_{\rho,\tau'}^n)\) for every \(\rho,n\);
 \item \(N_{n,C}(\tau)=N_{n,C}(\tau')\) for every \(n,C\);
 \item \(p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')\) for every \(n,C\).
\end{enumerate}
This is an equivalence of periodic data, not a conjugacy or switching
classification.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The normalized identity
\[
 -\Log_0P_{\rho,\tau}(z)
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\Tr(A_{\rho,\tau}^n)z^n/n
\]
gives (i)\(\Leftrightarrow\)(ii).  Expanding closed paths gives
\[
 \Tr(A_{\rho,\tau}^n)=\sum_C N_{n,C}(\tau)\chi_\rho(C),
\]
and the irreducible character table is invertible, proving
(ii)\(\Leftrightarrow\)(iii).  Finally,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-periodic-primitive-triangular}
 N_{n,C}=\sum_{d\mid n}d
   \sum_{\substack{D\in\operatorname{Conj}(G)\\D^{,n/d}=C}}p_{d,D}.
\end{equation}
The \(d=n\) term is \(np_{n,C}\); induction on \(n\) proves
(iii)\(\Leftrightarrow\)(iv).  These are the standard character and
necklace/Witt transforms of the periodic data.
\end{proof}

+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        collision_points: tuple[sp.Expr, ...] = ()
+    else:
+        roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+        collision_points = tuple(
+            root
+            for root in roots
+            if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+        )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound + 1,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= degree_bound,
+    }
+

codex
The first implementation passed, but the proof reveals a sharper count than the initial test encoded: normalization forces \(A(0)-B(0)=0\), so zero is always one root outside the admissible interval. A nontrivial certificate therefore has at most \(N-1\) positive collision radii, and \(N\), not \(N+1\), algebraic samples suffice. I’m tightening the test to that mathematically stronger contract before changing the verifier.

+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }

+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }

\begin{theorem}[Strict-gap determinant boundary lifting]
\label{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting}
Let \(A\) be a primitive non-negative integer matrix with Perron root
\(\lambda>1\), and put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\).  Let \(B,B'\) be integer matrices
of the same size such that, entrywise,
\[
 \abs{B_{ij}},\abs{B'_{ij}}\le A_{ij},
 \qquad B_{ij}\equiv B'_{ij}\equiv A_{ij}\pmod2,
\]
and suppose that \(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\).  Set
\[
 H(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}.
\]
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
 \item \(\Pi_x(H)=1\);
 \item there is a unique \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
 \[
  R(0)=R(x)=1,
  \qquad H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2}.
 \]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The strict gaps imply that both determinant polynomials are non-zero on a disk
\(\abs z<r\) for some \(x<r<1\).  They are positive on \([0,x]\), because
they are real, non-zero there, and equal one at zero.  Hence \(H>0\) on that
interval.  Define \(F\) by \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-product}.  By
\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, it is analytic on \(\abs z<r\), has
integer coefficients, and satisfies \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-equation}.
Crucially, the product normalization is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
 F(x)^2=\Pi_x(H),
\end{equation}
not \(F(x)=\Pi_x(H)\).

We now verify every hypothesis of Nishioka's special-value theorem
\cite[Theorem, p.~387]{Nishioka1982MahlerFunctionValues}.  Write the rational
function \(H\) in reduced form
\[
 H=\frac{\widehat P_0}{\widehat P_1},
 \qquad
 \widehat P_0,\widehat P_1\in\ZZ[z],
 \qquad
 \gcd(\widehat P_0,\widehat P_1)=1,
 \qquad
 \widehat P_0(0)=\widehat P_1(0)=1.
\]
The common factors removed here do not affect zero-freeness on \(\abs z<r\).
In the notation of the cited theorem, take
\[
 Tz=z^2,
 \qquad
 Q_0(z,u)=\widehat P_0(z),
 \qquad
 Q_1(z,u)=-\widehat P_1(z)u^2.
\]
Then the functional equation is exactly
\[
 Q_0(z,F(z))F(Tz)+Q_1(z,F(z))=0.
\]
The two polynomials \(Q_0,Q_1\) are relatively prime in
\(\overline{\QQ}[z,u]\): a common factor cannot contain \(u\), since
\(\widehat P_0(0)=1\), and the remaining assertion is the displayed
coprimality of \(\widehat P_0,\widehat P_1\).  Nishioka's auxiliary
polynomial \(g(z)\), obtained as a polynomial combination of the \(Q_i\)
and independent of \(u\), may therefore be chosen simply as
\(g(z)=Q_0(z,u)=\widehat P_0(z)\).

The numerical parameters are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
  p&=2, & N&=0, & n&=1, & m&=2,\\
  M&=\max\{p+N,m\}=2, & U&=1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus, with coefficient-growth exponent \(L=1\), her strict inequality is
\[
 M(p+N)n^2=2\cdot2\cdot1=4
 <2^{2+1/L}=8.
\]
It remains to check the arithmetic and orbit conditions, rather than merely
record the parameters.  Write \(F(z)=\sum_{h\ge0}a_hz^h\).  By
\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, all \(a_h\) lie in the fixed number
field \(\QQ\) and are algebraic integers.  Choose \(s\) with \(x<s<r\).
Cauchy's estimate on \(\abs z=s\) gives
\[
 \abs{a_h}\le \max_{\abs z=s}\abs{F(z)}\,s^{-h}.
\]
Hence Nishioka's coefficient-size and common-denominator bounds hold with
\(L=1\): the denominators are one and the logarithmic coefficient height is
at most linear in \(h\).  The evaluation point \(x=\lambda^{-1}\) is a
non-zero algebraic number and \(0<Ux<1\).  Moreover,
\[
 T^i x=x^{2^i}\ne0,
 \qquad
 g(T^i x)=\widehat P_0(x^{2^i})\ne0
 \quad(i\ge0),
\]
because \(0<x^{2^i}\le x<r\) and the reduced numerator is zero-free on
\(\abs z<r\).  Finally \(F(x)\) converges because \(F\) is analytic there.
All hypotheses of the cited theorem are therefore satisfied.  It follows
that if \(F\) were transcendental over \(\CC(z)\), then \(F(x)\) would be
transcendental.

Assume \(\textup{(i)}\).  Positivity and \eqref{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
give \(F(x)=1\), so the cited theorem forces \(F\) to be algebraic.  By
\Cref{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}, \(H=\delta R\) for the unique
normalized rational \(R\).  Now
\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} gives
\(1=\Pi_x(H)=R(x)^{-2}\) and \(R(x)>0\), hence \(R(x)=1\).  This proves
\(\textup{(ii)}\).  Conversely, \(\textup{(ii)}\) and
\eqref{eq:rational-mahler-telescope} give \(\textup{(i)}\), and the
same proposition gives uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope of the lifting theorem]
The determinant parity in \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} is essential
to the integrality step, so the theorem does not assert the converse for an
arbitrary positive rational \(H\).  Its realizable class is nevertheless broad.
Fix \(r\ge2\), an odd \(a>0\), and a positive even \(b\), and let \(A\) have
diagonal entries \(a\) and off-diagonal entries \(b\).  Then
\(\lambda=a+(r-1)b\).  Any diagonal \(B=\operatorname{diag}(c_i)\) and

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }
+
+

+

+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+Then either the primitive length--class profiles are identical, or
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+More precisely, if the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty and the
+profiles are not identical, the finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, equality at any \(N\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_N\in(0,x]\) forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover the
+entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N\) distinct algebraic radii while
+\(H\ne1\), this bound would be contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic
+data dictionary gives the asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}
+
 This mechanism is strictly weaker than full \(G\)-cospectrality, equivalently
 represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
 \eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and

+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+Then either the primitive length--class profiles are identical, or
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+More precisely, if the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty and the
+profiles are not identical, the finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, equality at any \(N\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_N\in(0,x]\) forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover the
+entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N\) distinct algebraic radii while
+\(H\ne1\), this bound would be contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic
+data dictionary gives the asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}
+
 This mechanism is strictly weaker than full \(G\)-cospectrality, equivalently
 represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
 \eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }
+

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)

+\]

+\[

+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]

+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:

+\end{equation}
+If the set in

+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(n\) is the size of the base matrix and
