+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+If the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty and the
+finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(n\) is the size of the base matrix and
+\[
+ N_*=(2n)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2n)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16n^3,
+\]
+then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\) forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
+the entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(n\), so reduction gives \(D\le2n\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}

 represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:

\begin{theorem}[Strict-gap determinant boundary lifting]
\label{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting}
Let \(A\) be a primitive non-negative integer matrix with Perron root
\(\lambda>1\), and put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\).  Let \(B,B'\) be integer matrices
of the same size such that, entrywise,
\[
 \abs{B_{ij}},\abs{B'_{ij}}\le A_{ij},
 \qquad B_{ij}\equiv B'_{ij}\equiv A_{ij}\pmod2,
\]
and suppose that \(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\).  Set
\[
 H(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}.
\]
For every algebraic number \(y\) with \(0<y\le x\), the following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
 \item \(\Pi_y(H)=1\);
 \item there is a unique \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
 \[
  R(0)=R(y)=1,
  \qquad H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2}.
 \]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The strict gaps imply that both determinant polynomials are non-zero on a disk
\(\abs z<r\) for some \(x<r<1\).  They are positive on \([0,x]\), because
they are real, non-zero there, and equal one at zero.  Hence \(H>0\) on that
interval.  Define \(F\) by \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-product}.  By
\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, it is analytic on \(\abs z<r\), has
integer coefficients, and satisfies \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-equation}.
Crucially, the product normalization is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
 F(y)^2=\Pi_y(H),
\end{equation}
not \(F(y)=\Pi_y(H)\).

We now verify every hypothesis of Nishioka's special-value theorem
\cite[Theorem, p.~387]{Nishioka1982MahlerFunctionValues}.  Write the rational
function \(H\) in reduced form
\[
 H=\frac{\widehat P_0}{\widehat P_1},
 \qquad
 \widehat P_0,\widehat P_1\in\ZZ[z],
 \qquad
 \gcd(\widehat P_0,\widehat P_1)=1,
 \qquad
 \widehat P_0(0)=\widehat P_1(0)=1.
\]
The common factors removed here do not affect zero-freeness on \(\abs z<r\).
In the notation of the cited theorem, take
\[
 Tz=z^2,
 \qquad
 Q_0(z,u)=\widehat P_0(z),
 \qquad
 Q_1(z,u)=-\widehat P_1(z)u^2.
\]
Then the functional equation is exactly
\[
 Q_0(z,F(z))F(Tz)+Q_1(z,F(z))=0.
\]
The two polynomials \(Q_0,Q_1\) are relatively prime in
\(\overline{\QQ}[z,u]\): a common factor cannot contain \(u\), since
\(\widehat P_0(0)=1\), and the remaining assertion is the displayed
coprimality of \(\widehat P_0,\widehat P_1\).  Nishioka's auxiliary
polynomial \(g(z)\), obtained as a polynomial combination of the \(Q_i\)
and independent of \(u\), may therefore be chosen simply as
\(g(z)=Q_0(z,u)=\widehat P_0(z)\).

The numerical parameters are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
  p&=2, & N&=0, & n&=1, & m&=2,\\
  M&=\max\{p+N,m\}=2, & U&=1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus, with coefficient-growth exponent \(L=1\), her strict inequality is
\[
 M(p+N)n^2=2\cdot2\cdot1=4
 <2^{2+1/L}=8.
\]
It remains to check the arithmetic and orbit conditions, rather than merely
record the parameters.  Write \(F(z)=\sum_{h\ge0}a_hz^h\).  By
\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, all \(a_h\) lie in the fixed number
field \(\QQ\) and are algebraic integers.  Choose \(s\) with \(x<s<r\).
Cauchy's estimate on \(\abs z=s\) gives
\[
 \abs{a_h}\le \max_{\abs z=s}\abs{F(z)}\,s^{-h}.
\]
Hence Nishioka's coefficient-size and common-denominator bounds hold with
\(L=1\): the denominators are one and the logarithmic coefficient height is
at most linear in \(h\).  The evaluation point \(y\) is a non-zero algebraic
number and \(0<Uy<1\).  Moreover,
\[
 T^i y=y^{2^i}\ne0,
 \qquad
 g(T^i y)=\widehat P_0(y^{2^i})\ne0
 \quad(i\ge0),
\]
because \(0<y^{2^i}\le y\le x<r\) and the reduced numerator is zero-free
on \(\abs z<r\).  Finally \(F(y)\) converges because \(F\) is analytic
there.
All hypotheses of the cited theorem are therefore satisfied.  It follows
that if \(F\) were transcendental over \(\CC(z)\), then \(F(y)\) would be
transcendental.

Assume \(\textup{(i)}\).  Positivity and \eqref{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
give \(F(y)=1\), so the cited theorem forces \(F\) to be algebraic.  By
\Cref{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}, \(H=\delta R\) for the unique
normalized rational \(R\).  Now
\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} gives
\(1=\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) and \(R(y)>0\), hence \(R(y)=1\).  This proves
\(\textup{(ii)}\).  Conversely, \(\textup{(ii)}\) and
\eqref{eq:rational-mahler-telescope} give \(\textup{(i)}\), and the
same proposition gives uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope of the lifting theorem]
The determinant parity in \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} is essential
to the integrality step, so the theorem does not assert the converse for an
arbitrary positive rational \(H\).  Its realizable class is nevertheless broad.
Fix \(r\ge2\), an odd \(a>0\), and a positive even \(b\), and let \(A\) have
diagonal entries \(a\) and off-diagonal entries \(b\).  Then
\(\lambda=a+(r-1)b\).  Any diagonal \(B=\operatorname{diag}(c_i)\) and
\(B'=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\), with odd
\(\abs{c_i},\abs{d_i}\le a\), satisfies the same-base compatibility and
strict gaps, and realizes
\[
 H(z)=\frac{\prod_i(1-c_i z)}{\prod_i(1-d_i z)}.
\]
\end{remark}

       \operatorname{per}(A[I,I])
 \le n^ka_*^k\le(na_*)^n,
\]
and the same estimate holds for \(B'\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:same-base-effective-input-bounds}; substituting those inequalities
in \eqref{eq:effective-mahler-height-bound} proves
\eqref{eq:same-base-effective-height-bound}.  Coprimality is stated because
the numerical bounds of \Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} apply
to the reduced input pair.  A non-coprime determinant ratio may first be
cancelled, but no unchanged-height assertion for the uncancelled pair is
being made here.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
Let \(G=C_2\), and let
\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
\[
 \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
 :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
 \qquad(0<y\le x),
\]
where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
\[
 H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
\]
in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).

If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
\[
 L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
 \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
\]
\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
 \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
\end{equation}
If the set in
\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty and the
finite Pad\'e procedure of
\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
\[
 R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
 \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
 \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
\]
for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
 \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
 =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, if \(n\) is the size of the base matrix and
\[
 N_*=(2n)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2n)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16n^3,
\]
then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\) forces
\[
 p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
 \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
\]
Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
the entire primitive length--class profile.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
 \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
 =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
 =-\log\Pi_y(H)
 \qquad(0<y\le x).
\end{equation}
The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
\([0,x]\), and the series in
\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
\[
 \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
\]

If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).

Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
\[
 H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
 \qquad R(y_0)=1.
\]
The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).

For every real \(0<y\le x\),
\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
\[
 \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 R(y)=1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.

Each determinant has degree at most \(n\), so reduction gives \(D\le2n\).
The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
\end{proof}

This mechanism is strictly weaker than full \(G\)-cospectrality, equivalently
represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
\eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and
\eqref{eq:c2-collision-second-determinant} are different.  Represented
cospectrality in every irreducible representation instead requires equality
of the full twisted spectra and therefore preserves the complete periodic profile
\cite{BoyleSchmieding2017FiniteGroupExtensions,
CavaleriDonno2022Cospectrality}.

We next delimit the finite minimality assertion.  A \emph{regular polynomial
\(C_2\)-certificate} is a tuple \((A,B,B',Q)\) in which \(A\) is a primitive
\(m\)-out-regular integral adjacency matrix, \(B,B'\) are compatible sign
blocks, \(Q\in\ZZ[z]\) is non-constant with \(Q(0)=Q(1/m)=1\), both sign
blocks have spectral radius less than \(m\), and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-polynomial-certificate}
 \det(I-zB)=Q(z^2),
 \qquad
 \det(I-zB')=Q(z)^2.
\end{equation}
Its complexity is ordered lexicographically as
\[
 \bigl(2,\deg Q,|V|,m,|E|\bigr).
\]

\begin{proposition}[Minimality in the regular polynomial certificate class]
\label{prop:c2-certificate-minimality}
The certificate in \Cref{thm:c2-boundary-collision} has complexity
\((2,2,4,4,16)\), and this is the least complexity of a regular polynomial
\(C_2\)-certificate.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first coordinate is fixed by the non-trivial binary group.  Since
\(Q(0)=Q(1/m)=1\), a non-constant \(Q\) cannot have degree one, so
\(\deg Q\ge2\).  If \(\deg Q=2\), then \(Q(z^2)\) has degree four, whereas
\(\deg\det(I-zB)\le |V|\); hence \(|V|\ge4\).

It remains to exclude \(m=2,3\) at \(\deg Q=2\) and \(|V|=4\).  Write
\begin{equation}\label{eq:minimality-q-form}
 Q(z)=1-kz+kmz^2,
 \qquad k\in\ZZ\setminus\{0\},
\end{equation}
which follows from \(Q(1/m)=1\).  When \(m=2\), the characteristic
polynomial forced by the second identity in
\eqref{eq:regular-polynomial-certificate} is
\((x^2-kx+2k)^2\).  If its roots have modulus strictly less than two, their
product gives \(|k|<2\).  The choice \(k=-1\) has a root \(-2\), and
\(k=0\) makes \(Q\) constant; therefore strict gap forces \(k=1\).

There are exactly ten non-negative integral four-entry rows of sum two,
namely \(2e_i\) and \(e_i+e_j\) for \(i<j\).  We exhaust the resulting
\(10^4\) matrices.  Primitivity is decided exactly by testing positivity of
a power through exponent ten, the four-dimensional Wielandt bound.  This
leaves \(2208\) primitive base matrices.  For each such matrix, every
compatible signed entry is enumerated from
\[
 B_{ij}\in\{-A_{ij},-A_{ij}+2,\ldots,A_{ij}\}.
\]
For an integral \(4\times4\) matrix, put \(t_r=\Tr(B^r)\).  Newton's
identities give
\[
 \det(I-zB)=1-t_1z+\frac{t_1^2-t_2}{2}z^2
 -\frac{t_1^3-3t_1t_2+2t_3}{6}z^3+\det(B)z^4.
\]
Thus the two target polynomials
\(1-z^2+2z^4\) and \((1-z+2z^2)^2\) are tested by the integer quadruples
\[
 (t_1,t_2,t_3,\det B)=(0,2,0,2),
 \qquad (2,-6,-10,4),
\]
respectively.  The exhaustive integer enumeration finds \(48\) primitive
bases supporting the first target and no primitive base supporting the
second.  Hence no certificate exists for \(m=2\).  The enumeration and all
counts are reproduced by the exact-arithmetic verifier cited in
\Cref{sec:exactness}.

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }
+

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+If the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty and the
+finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(n\) is the size of the base matrix and
+\[
+ N_*=(2n)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2n)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16n^3,
+\]
+then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\) forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
+the entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(n\), so reduction gives \(D\le2n\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}
+

 represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
 \eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+If the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty, then the
+finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(v\) is the size of the base matrix and
+\[
+ N_*=(2v)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2v)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16v^3,
+\]
+then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\), meaning
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y_i)=0\) for every \(i\), forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
+the entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(v\), so reduction gives \(D\le2v\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}

 represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
 \eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+If the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty, then the
+finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(v\) is the size of the base matrix and
+\[
+ N_*=(2v)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2v)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16v^3,
+\]
+then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\), meaning
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y_i)=0\) for every \(i\), forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
+the entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(v\), so reduction gives \(D\le2v\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

The theorem of Mohamed and Noorani requires two independent corrections.
Primitivity of the base does not imply Frobenius equidistribution: the
trivial \(C_2\)-cocycle shows that an extension-level
transitivity/aperiodicity condition is necessary.  Under the strict twisted
gap used here, the exponent is \(|C|/|G|\).  At the constant level, the
Frobenius-class product fixes the primitive label \(g_\gamma\), whereas the
periodic Artin logarithm replaces it by \(g_\gamma^r\) on the \(r\)-fold
traversal.  The correct coordinate is therefore \(F_\rho\), with the
finite-determinant formula in \eqref{eq:perron-fixed-determinant}; the strict-gap
\(S_3\) sign channel proves that it cannot generally be replaced by
\(L_\rho\).

The discrepancy is universal at the identity class, not confined to the
\(S_3\) witness.  The quotient-cover factor in
\eqref{eq:identity-class-universal-error} is strictly greater than one for
every non-trivial strict-gap extension and records precisely the primitive
orbits whose lifts close only after repeated traversal.  After the constant is
corrected, \eqref{eq:harmonic-renormalized-product} separates the universal
harmonic factor from an exponentially small system-dependent remainder.

The vector of corrected constants is nevertheless not an inverse invariant
of the primitive class profile.  The fixed-graph \(C_2\) pair in
\Cref{thm:c2-boundary-collision} has different length-one data but identical
constants, because the dyadic boundary functional annihilates a non-trivial
determinant coboundary at the Perron point.  This collision is strictly weaker
than full \(G\)-cospectrality.  In the realizable same-base strict-gap
determinant-ratio class, \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} identifies this
kernel exactly with the normalized rational coboundaries; its parity hypothesis
prevents an extension of that statement here to arbitrary positive rational
functions.  Within its coprime polynomial input class,
\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} decides this rational
coboundary condition by one finite Pad\'e system and supplies explicit output
bounds; \Cref{cor:same-base-effective-rational-mahler} records the compatible
matrix specialization.  Retaining an analytic radial profile
on a set with an interior accumulation point removes the loss by
\Cref{thm:radial-profile-recovery}; no claim of minimality is attached to that
analytic enhancement.

For a homogeneous union of classes, the downstream constant is
\eqref{eq:homogeneous-union-constant}.  The M\"obius transform used to obtain
it is standard necklace/Witt calculus; the paper-specific point is its use on
the fixed-label coordinate before Adams powering.  The appendices record only
the determinant-derived radial convention and established periodic-data and
gain-graph translations needed to fix the scope of the main result.


 succeeded in 209ms:
does not claim those scalar coefficients as new, but supplies the exact
harmonic normalization and exponential remainder for all fixed-label unions
under the twisted gap.

length-one class counts differ.  The equality follows from the exact
determinant coboundary \(Q(z^2)/Q(z)^2\), with \(Q(1/4)=1\), rather than from
numerical approximation.  The example is minimal in the regular polynomial
certificate class of \Cref{prop:c2-certificate-minimality}.  Within the
same-base strict-gap determinant-ratio class,
\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} proves that these are all the isolated
boundary collisions: vanishing of the single boundary functional is equivalent
to a unique normalized rational Mahler certificate.  The proof uses
determinant parity together with Nishioka's published critical special-value
theorem, and does not assert the corresponding converse for arbitrary positive
rational functions.  The resulting rational certificate is fully effective:
\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} gives explicit degree and
height bounds and a complete finite Pad\'e decision procedure, while
\Cref{cor:same-base-effective-rational-mahler} specializes the input bounds to
compatible matrices on one base.  Finally,
\Cref{thm:radial-profile-recovery} proves that equality of the subcritical
class Euler profiles on any set with an interior accumulation point recovers
all primitive length--class data.  No optimality assertion is made for this
profile hypothesis.

\subsection{Scope of the background appendix}

Equality of all represented spectra is the finite-group gain-graph notion of
\(G\)-cospectrality, and its translation to conjugacy-class periodic data is
established context
\cite{CavaleriDAngeliDonno2021BalanceGainGraphs,
CavaleriDonno2022Cospectrality,BoyleSchmieding2017FiniteGroupExtensions}.

 succeeded in 224ms:
\[
 L_\rho(z)=\sum_{r\geq1}\Pi_{\psi^r\chi_\rho}(z^r)/r,
 \qquad (\psi^r\chi_\rho)(g)=\chi_\rho(g^r),
\]
whereas the class product repeats the scalar weight while keeping the
primitive label fixed.  Its coordinate is therefore
\(F_\rho(z)=\sum_{r\geq1}\Pi_{\chi_\rho}(z^r)/r\).  Under the strict twisted
spectral gap, we prove an Adams--M\"obius determinant formula for
\(F_\rho(\lambda^{-1})\) and hence for every class-product constant.

This corrects two independent defects in the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani
(1999).  First, mixing of the base alone does not imply Frobenius
equidistribution: an extension-level aperiodicity condition, imposed here as
the strict twisted gap, is also necessary.  Second, their constant replaces
\(\chi_\rho(g_\gamma)\) by \(\chi_\rho(g_\gamma^r)\) in the \(r\)-th
logarithmic term.  A trivial \(C_2\)-cocycle disproves the exponent under base
mixing alone, while a strict-gap \(S_3\) extension disproves the asserted
Artin coordinate.  Under the stated gap hypothesis the exponent is
\(|C|/|G|\), and the non-trivial constant coordinates are the fixed-label
values above.  We further identify the exact positive quotient-cover factor
missed by the Artin substitution, proving that it strictly underestimates the
identity-class constant in every non-trivial strict-gap extension.  Harmonic
renormalization gives an exponentially accurate product asymptotic for every
union of Frobenius classes.  Finally, an exact four-vertex \(C_2\) pair shows
that all class constants together do not determine the primitive class
profile, even under strict gap; an analytic radial profile with an interior
accumulation set restores that profile.
\end{abstract}

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+If the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty, then the
+finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(v\) is the size of the base matrix and
+\[
+ N_*=(2v)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2v)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16v^3,
+\]
+then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\), meaning
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y_i)=0\) for every \(i\), forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
+the entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(v\), so reduction gives \(D\le2v\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}

 represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
 \eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }
+

+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(v\), so reduction gives \(D\le2v\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }
+

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+If the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty, then the
+finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(v\) is the size of the base matrix and
+\[
+ N_*=(2v)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2v)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16v^3,
+\]
+then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\), meaning
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y_i)=0\) for every \(i\), forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
+the entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(v\), so reduction gives \(D\le2v\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }
+

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+If the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty, then the
+finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(v\) is the size of the base matrix and
+\[
+ N_*=(2v)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2v)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16v^3,
+\]
+then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\), meaning
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y_i)=0\) for every \(i\), forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
+the entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(v\), so reduction gives \(D\le2v\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}
+

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }
+

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+If the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty, then the
+finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(v\) is the size of the base matrix and
+\[
+ N_*=(2v)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2v)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16v^3,
+\]
+then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\), meaning
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y_i)=0\) for every \(i\), forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
+the entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(v\), so reduction gives \(D\le2v\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}
+

 represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
 \eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and

+def finite_radial_collision_audit(
+    p_zero_expression: sp.Expr,
+    p_one_expression: sp.Expr,
+    interval_end: sp.Expr,
+) -> dict[str, sp.Expr | int | bool | tuple[sp.Expr, ...]]:
+    """Extract the radial collision set from a normalized Mahler certificate."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    certificate = effective_rational_mahler_coboundary(
+        p_zero_expression, p_one_expression
+    )
+    if certificate is None:
+        raise ValueError("the input ratio has no normalized rational certificate")
+
+    collision_polynomial = sp.factor(
+        certificate["numerator"] - certificate["denominator"]
+    )
+    if collision_polynomial == 0:
+        raise ValueError("the identity ratio has every admissible point as a collision")
+    roots = sp.real_roots(sp.Poly(collision_polynomial, z, domain=sp.QQ))
+    collision_points = tuple(
+        root
+        for root in roots
+        if bool(root > 0) and bool(root <= interval_end)
+    )
+    degree_bound = int(certificate["degree_bound"])
+    collision_bound = degree_bound - 1
+    return {
+        **certificate,
+        "collision_polynomial": collision_polynomial,
+        "collision_points": collision_points,
+        "degree_bound": degree_bound,
+        "collision_bound": collision_bound,
+        "sample_budget": degree_bound,
+        "collision_count_within_bound": len(collision_points) <= collision_bound,
+    }
+

+\begin{theorem}[Effective finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
+\label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
+Let \(G=C_2\), and let
+\(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
+directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Suppose that
+\(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x),
+\]
+where the value at \(x\) is the strict-gap radial value.  Write
+\[
+ H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
+      =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
+\]
+in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
+\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
+
+If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
+length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
+\[
+ L=\lfloor\log_2D\rfloor,
+ \qquad N=D^2(2^{L+1}-1).
+\]
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
+ \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x]:
+          \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
+\end{equation}
+If the set in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty, then the
+finite Pad\'e procedure of
+\Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
+\[
+ R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
+ \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
+ \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
+\]
+for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
+ \{y\in(0,x]:\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
+ =\{y\in(0,x]:A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
+\end{equation}
+Consequently, if \(v\) is the size of the base matrix and
+\[
+ N_*=(2v)^2\bigl(2^{\lfloor\log_2(2v)\rfloor+1}-1\bigr)<16v^3,
+\]
+then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct algebraic radii
+\(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x]\), meaning
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y_i)=0\) for every \(i\), forces
+\[
+ p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
+\]
+Equivalently, \(N_*\) samples of both radial class Euler profiles recover
+the entire primitive length--class profile.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
+\(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
+\eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
+therefore gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
+ =-\log\Pi_y(H)
+ \qquad(0<y\le x).
+\end{equation}
+The strict gaps make both determinant polynomials zero-free on a disk
+strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).  They are consequently positive on
+\([0,x]\), and the series in
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.  Thus
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
+\]
+
+If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
+both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
+primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
+
+Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
+\eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
+choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
+\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
+ \qquad R(y_0)=1.
+\]
+The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
+\(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
+
+For every real \(0<y\le x\),
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
+\(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
+\[
+ \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ R(y)=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
+\]
+which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
+the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
+\(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
+roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
+
+Each determinant has degree at most \(v\), so reduction gives \(D\le2v\).
+The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
+\(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
+distinct algebraic radii while \(H\ne1\), the bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be
+contradicted.  Thus \(H=1\), and the periodic data dictionary gives the
+asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
+the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
+\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
+\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
+\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to simultaneous equality of the two
+radial class Euler profiles at \(y\), proving the last assertion.
+\end{proof}
+
